title: Sangchul's Verdict
description:
You went in on Sangchul's tip and it paid off.
Today Sangchul called.
"Minjun. See? What did I tell you."
There was pride in his voice.

choices.result_text:
Sangchul said 'Let me treat you this time.'
Over dinner, the next investment came up.
One tip was turning into trust.

Sangchul paused and said 'Luck is skill too.'
Whether that's true or not — the next one will decide.

title: Since That Tip
description:
You followed Sangchul's tip and took a loss.
Today you ran into Sangchul at another gathering.
Your eyes met.
For a moment, it was awkward.

choices.text: Speak first. "That call was my decision."
choices.result_text:
Sangchul said 'I'm sorry about how it turned out.'
'No — it was my choice.'
A short silence, and it ended like adults.
The relationship was still alive.

choices.text: Pretend you didn't see each other
choices.result_text:
You both looked away.
The awkwardness kept coming back later.
Losing the money was less uncomfortable than the damaged connection.

title: A Text from Daeun
description:
A few months ago you were there for Daeun when things were hard.
Today a text from Daeun.
'Minjun. I was thinking about that time.
How have you been?'

choices.result_text:
Daeun replied 'Sounds good' right away.
Being there for her then brought this.
Good things come back this way sometimes.

Daeun sent 'Good to hear :)'
The conversation ended quickly.
There was something there — but the distance didn't close.

title: The Distance That Grew
description:
You'd kept drawing lines around Daeun.
Today you heard through a mutual friend.
Daeun had moved to a different neighborhood.

choices.result_text:
You sent a text. 'Heard you moved. How are you?'
Only the read receipt appeared.
No reply.
You were the one who drew the lines.

You left it.
You thought you wanted a comfortable distance — but this wasn't distance, it was just far.

title: What Daeun Remembers
description:
There was that conversation where Daeun understood your situation.
Today you ran into her at the same café by coincidence.
Daeun smiled and waved first.

choices.result_text:
You talked for an hour.
Daeun said 'I appreciated that you were honest with me back then.'
Being understood then — brought this moment.

choices.text: Just say hello and go back to your seat
choices.result_text:
You exchanged a greeting.
Went back to your own tables.
You knew she was a good person.

title: Daeun's Last Question
description:
You'd brushed off Daeun's words several times.
Today Daeun asked directly.
"Minjun. Am I bothering you?
You can be honest with me."

choices.text: "It's not that. I just don't have the bandwidth right now."
choices.result_text:
Daeun was quiet for a moment, then said 'That's a relief.'
It took a long time to say something honest.
But maybe it wasn't too late.

choices.text: "No, I've just been busy." Deflect again.
choices.result_text:
Daeun said 'I see' and stopped asking.
That look — it seemed like 'that's enough for me.'

title: The Job from That Introduction
description:
You returned the wallet, and that person offered a job referral.
You ended up reaching out and did the interview.
Today is three months since joining that company.

choices.text: It's a good fit. Keep going.
choices.result_text:
A small company, but the people were good.
The owner said 'I want to work together for a long time.'
One wallet led to all this.
Good things do come back like this sometimes.

choices.text: It's not a good fit. Start looking elsewhere.
choices.result_text:
It wasn't a good fit.
But the referral became a line on the resume.
Connections leave traces even when the result isn't what you hoped.

title: That Contact
description:
When you returned the wallet, you turned down the job offer.
You'd probably deleted the contact — but on a whim you searched.
The company name came up.
It looked pretty decent.

choices.result_text:
'I'm sorry for turning you down back then. Is the position still open?'
A reply came after a long wait. 'We've already filled it.'
Disappointing.
But reaching out was still the right call.

choices.text: Close it. Do well with what you have.
choices.result_text:
You closed the tab.
There was a reason you said no back then.
That reason still holds.

title: Another Nameless Report
description:
Back then you'd pushed back on the credit claim and ended up backing down.
Today the same situation came up again.
The team lead submitted the whole team's work under their own name.

choices.result_text:
'Team lead, this material was mine — I'd appreciate it if my name was included.'
The team lead stiffened for a moment. '...Fine.'
If you back down once, you keep backing down. Now you know.

You let it go again.
The team lead will do it next time too.
If you don't draw a line, there is no line.

title: Team Lead's 1:1
description:
A month ago you went over your team lead's head to claim credit.
Today the team lead requested a 1:1 meeting.

choices.text: Walk in and take it head-on
choices.result_text:
The team lead was cold. 'Going forward, please go through me.'
But after that, your name wasn't left off.
There was a cost — but something was gained too.

choices.text: Apologize to the team lead first
choices.result_text:
'Skipping the process was my mistake.'
The team lead's expression softened. 'Thank you for saying that.'
But next time, the name might be missing again.
Apologizing and changing things are different.

title: Six Months Without Hyeonsu
description:
Half a year since you cut the gambling connection with Hyeonsu.
Today Hyeonsu posted in a group chat.
'I got a job. Completely done with betting.'
An unfamiliar company name.

choices.result_text:
You pressed like.
Hyeonsu sent a short reply. 'You doing okay too?'
You just said 'Yeah.'
The distance that grew between you seemed to suit both of you.

You didn't do anything.
You were genuinely glad Hyeonsu was doing well.
Some relationships don't need to be close to be good.

title: The Morning After
description:
You stayed at the company dinner until 2 AM.
The next morning the alarm went off and your eyes wouldn't open.
Ten minutes before you had to leave.

choices.text: Force yourself up and go in
choices.result_text:
You barely made it to your seat.
The team lead walked by and said 'Good work last night.'
Body felt awful, face relaxed.
This is office life.

You filed for half a day.
The team lead said 'Last night was rough, huh.'
Body first. Figured it out late.

title: The Atmosphere Since Then
description:
Two weeks since you took a half-day instead of going to the dinner.
The team dynamic seems subtly different.
Not sure exactly what changed.

choices.text: Ask directly. "Did I make things weird?"
choices.result_text:
A coworker said 'No, nothing like that. I just learned you're the type who keeps your distance.'
The type who keeps their distance.
Not sure if that's good or bad.

You stopped thinking about it.
Something did shift.
But that's not your fault.

title: The Team Lead Knew
description:
The day you slipped out of the company dinner early.
Today the team lead stopped you in the hallway.
"Minjun. You left early last time, right?"

choices.result_text:
The team lead said 'Just let me know ahead of time next time.'
Not sure if that was a scolding or consideration.
Either way, it passed.

The team lead said 'Alright. Let me know next time.'
One small lie.
It passed this time.

title: Father's Time
description:
You found out your father's health had gotten much worse.
You should see him often while it's still a good time — your aunt told you something like that.
You searched the bus schedule to your hometown.

choices.result_text:
Your father was waiting at the door.
You had two bowls of rice.
On the bus back, you couldn't do anything for a long time.
Visiting often is right. That's right.

You marked it on the calendar.
Next month.
The words 'while it's still a good time' kept running through your head.

title: The Pace of Reconciliation
description:
Eight months since you started making things right with your father.
It was awkward at first — but now calling feels natural.
Today your father called first.
No reason in particular.

choices.result_text:
Forty minutes.
Nothing specific said.
Dad hung up first. 'Sleep well.'
This is how reconciliation completes.
Without a single dramatic moment.

choices.text: "Dad, I'm a bit busy right now. I'll call you back."
choices.result_text:
Dad said 'Okay, you're busy' and hung up.
You called back later.
He picked up immediately.
You realized he'd been waiting.
